title: 3rd Stopping Place 3rd Truth The Truth Of Disposing And Administering

questions.question: What is the name of the Third Truth in this passage?
questions.answer: The Truth of Disposing and Administering.

questions.question: What big things are mentioned as being managed?
questions.answer: The sky bodies, the natural elements, and the creatures on earth.

questions.question: How are the creatures on earth described?
questions.answer: They are needy and weak.

questions.question: What does the passage say these different things do with each other?
questions.answer: They help each other and are managed together.

questions.question: What does the world become like under this perfect rule?
questions.answer: Like a great kingdom, a beautiful city, and a lovely palace.

questions.question: Which season is used to show one page of this rule and care?
questions.answer: Spring.

questions.question: In the example, how many different groups are in the army?
questions.answer: Four hundred thousand.

questions.question: How does the commander do this work?
questions.answer: In the right way, at the right time, with no mix-up.

questions.question: What would happen if another cause tried to do this huge job?
questions.answer: The balance would break and confusion would happen.

questions.question: In the real world, what does the unseen hand make every spring?
questions.answer: A great army of four hundred thousand kinds of living things.

questions.question: What happens in autumn to many plants and animals?
questions.answer: Three hundred thousand kinds are sent away from their duties.

questions.question: What main idea is taught in the Third Truth?
questions.answer: Allah manages the world with perfect order.

questions.question: Does the passage speak about only small things or both great and small things?
questions.answer: Both great and small things.

questions.question: Which great things are named first?
questions.answer: The huge moving bodies in the sky.

questions.question: Which smaller things are named with them?
questions.answer: The creatures living on earth.

questions.question: Why is this amazing, based on the passage?
questions.answer: Because very different things are all cared for together.

questions.question: What picture is used for the world at the end of that management?
questions.answer: A perfect kingdom, a grand city, and a decorated palace.

questions.question: Why does the passage use a commander and army example?
questions.answer: To help us understand the huge and careful management.

questions.question: How many kinds are in the example army?
questions.answer: Four hundred thousand.

questions.question: Name two things each group receives in the example.
questions.answer: Clothing and weapons.

questions.question: Name two more things each group receives in the example.
questions.answer: Instructions and pay.

questions.question: What does it mean that all this is done at the proper time?
questions.answer: Everything is given when needed, not too early or late.

questions.question: What does the example teach about ordinary causes?
questions.answer: They cannot do such a great job.

questions.question: What season shows this real-life army most clearly?
questions.answer: Spring.

questions.question: What happens to many species in autumn?
questions.answer: They are dismissed and pass away.

questions.question: What is being proved by the orderly running of the world in this passage?
questions.answer: Allah’s unity and oneness.

questions.question: What word in the title means taking care of affairs?
questions.answer: Administering.

questions.question: What two qualities are named for the administration besides power?
questions.answer: Order and balance.

questions.question: What kinds of things are ruled with this order?
questions.answer: The heavens, the elements, and living things on earth.

questions.question: What does the passage say these things do for one another?
questions.answer: They give help to one another.

questions.question: If many unrelated powers were in charge, what would happen?
questions.answer: There would be disorder and confusion.

questions.question: What shows the commander’s greatness in the example?
questions.answer: He gives every group what it needs in the right way.

questions.question: What mistake does the example say another cause would make?
questions.answer: It would ruin the balance.

questions.question: In the real world, what is like that giant army?
questions.answer: The many species that appear in spring.

questions.question: How many species are mentioned in that spring army?
questions.answer: Four hundred thousand.

questions.question: In autumn, how many species are said to be sent away?
questions.answer: Three hundred thousand.

questions.question: Are these gifts given with mistakes or perfectly?
questions.answer: They are given perfectly.

questions.question: What season is used as a special lesson in this passage?
questions.answer: Spring.

questions.question: Before speaking about spring, what does the passage say about the whole world?
questions.answer: It is managed like a perfect kingdom.

questions.question: What other two pictures are given for the world?
questions.answer: A magnificent city and a decorated palace.

questions.question: In the comparison, what kind of leader is imagined?
questions.answer: A wonderful conqueror and commander.

questions.question: What makes his work so hard?
questions.answer: He has to care for four hundred thousand different groups.

questions.question: What does this teach about the springtime world?
questions.answer: Each kind of creature is cared for in its own way.

questions.question: What phrase shows that this work is beyond normal causes?
questions.answer: An unseen hand does it.

questions.question: What does the unseen hand do every spring?
questions.answer: It creates and runs a great army of living kinds.

questions.question: What are plants and animals compared to in this picture?
questions.answer: Soldiers with duties.

questions.question: What happens to many of them in autumn?
questions.answer: They are released from duty through death.

questions.question: What happens again in spring?
questions.answer: Many forms of life return.

questions.question: How many examples of rising again are made in a short time?
questions.answer: Three hundred thousand.

questions.question: What are the other three parts of the tree named?
questions.answer: The tree itself, its flowers, and its fruits.

questions.question: What does “without confusion” tell us?
questions.answer: Everything is done in a clear, organized way.

questions.question: What does the Third Truth help us notice in the world?
questions.answer: Careful rule and planning.

questions.question: Is this rule described as weak or mighty?
questions.answer: Mighty.

questions.question: What is one sign that this rule is balanced?
questions.answer: Very different things are managed together properly.

questions.question: Which two places are especially mentioned?
questions.answer: The heavens and the earth.

questions.question: How are the creatures of earth described in a humble way?
questions.answer: As weak and needy.

questions.question: What does it mean when the passage says they help each other?
questions.answer: Different parts of creation work together.

questions.question: What example is given to make this easier to picture?
questions.answer: A commander caring for a huge army.

questions.question: What is special about the army groups?
questions.answer: They are many and all different.

questions.question: What five kinds of needs are named for those groups?
questions.answer: Clothing, weapons, instructions, release, and pay.

questions.question: How well are these needs provided?
questions.answer: Fully and without mistakes.

questions.question: What does this say about the one doing the work?
questions.answer: He has amazing power.

questions.question: What would happen if something else tried to do that work?
questions.answer: Disorder would begin.

questions.question: What real event in nature matches this army picture?
questions.answer: The coming of living species in spring.

questions.question: How many species are mentioned?
questions.answer: Four hundred thousand.

questions.question: What happens to most of them in autumn?
questions.answer: Three hundred thousand leave their duties.

questions.question: What is death called for them in this picture?
questions.answer: Going on leave.

questions.question: Why is the tree a helpful example for kids to picture?
questions.answer: We can see its leaves, flowers, and fruits come again.

questions.question: When we see all this order, what should we understand?
questions.answer: Allah is One and has power over everything.

questions.question: What is the full title of the truth in this passage?
questions.answer: The Third Truth: the Truth of Disposing and Administering.

questions.question: What does the passage say is complete in this administration?
questions.answer: Order and balance.

questions.question: Are only peaceful things managed, or also powerful and fast-moving things?
questions.answer: Also powerful and fast-moving things.

questions.question: What powerful things are named?
questions.answer: The heavenly bodies and the elements.

questions.question: What gentle lesson is given about the earth’s creatures?
questions.answer: Even weak creatures are cared for.

questions.question: How are all these things treated together?
questions.answer: They are managed jointly and made to support one another.

questions.question: What three word-pictures are used for the world?
questions.answer: A kingdom, a city, and a palace.

questions.question: What small part of this huge rule does the passage choose to show?
questions.answer: What happens in spring on earth.

questions.question: In the comparison, why is the commander amazing?
questions.answer: He handles many different groups perfectly.

questions.question: What number of groups is named there?
questions.answer: Four hundred thousand.

questions.question: What is important about how each group is treated?
questions.answer: Each one gets its own needs met correctly.

questions.question: What time clue is repeated in the comparison?
questions.answer: Everything is done at the right time.

questions.question: What does the passage say would happen if another cause reached in?
questions.answer: It would spoil the balance and make confusion.

questions.question: In real life, who makes the spring army?
questions.answer: An unseen hand.

questions.question: What is this spring army made of?
questions.answer: Different species of plants and animals.

questions.question: What does autumn do to many of these species?
questions.answer: It sends them away from their work.

questions.question: What does spring do after that?
questions.answer: It brings many of them back in orderly ways.

questions.question: What four parts of a tree show repeated renewal?
questions.answer: The tree, leaves, flowers, and fruits.
